headline: Bangladesh outraged over India allowing Hasina's media interaction in New Delhi
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the move is an insult to the July Revolution's martyrs and a violation of Bangladesh's sovereignty.
details: Bangladesh has expressed deep anger after India allowed former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that Hasina and her associates used the platform to make 'poisonous' remarks against the state and people of Bangladesh.

// The Ministry noted that India was informed beforehand about the potential negative impact such an event could have on the process of rebuilding bilateral relations, yet the interaction was still permitted.
The government described the move as an insult to the martyrs of the July Revolution and a violation of Bangladesh's sovereignty, especially as the nation marks the anniversary of the uprising.
The Ministry also asserted that Hasina and her associates have no place in the politics of Bangladesh, now or in the future, following the atrocities committed during the fascist regime.
Bangladesh has repeatedly requested India to extradite Hasina under the 2013 extradition treaty, but the Ministry stated that the Indian government has yet to provide a response.
The statement concluded that allowing Hasina to speak publicly under any pretext is deeply hurtful to the people of Bangladesh and damaging to the development of friendly bilateral ties.

headline_marked: Petrol bomb [[hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house]] in Magura
headline: Petrol bomb hurled at Shakib Al Hasan's house in Magura
summary: Attackers targeted the iron gate of the former cricketer and former MP's residence on Wednesday night.
details: Miscreants hurled a petrol bomb and a cocktail at the gate of the house of Shakib Al Hasan, a former MP and former captain of the Bangladesh national cricket team, in Magura.
The incident occurred on Wednesday night at Shakib's residence located at Keshab Mor.
According to police, the explosive-like objects were thrown at the upper part of the iron gate on the south side of the house.
The fire was extinguished shortly after the attack, and no major damage or injuries were reported.
A team from the Magura Sadar Police Station arrived at the scene following the report and has since deployed police personnel for security.
Police stated that there is currently no information regarding who carried out the attack.
An investigation is underway to determine the exact cause of the incident and the nature of the explosives used.
